Stage 1 Problem Specification Read the client problem as a real brief and turn it into a set of success criteria. 1 pages Stage 2 Planning and Database Design Move from interface planning into tables, fields, normalisation, relationships, and testing. 5 pages Stage 3 Build Foundations Set up the stack, learn the syntax families, and write schema.sql and init_db.py before the live features begin. 5 pages Stage 4 Feature Build Sequence Implement the project in a strict feature order, one controlled change at a time. 10 pages Stage 5 Non-Standard Algorithm Design the tagging logic in plain English before you attempt any code. 1 pages Stage 6 Database Extension Extend the data model for many-to-many tagging and verify that the design still holds. 1 pages
1 Planning documents Wireframes, screen planning, field mapping, and planning decisions. 2 Normalisation workshop Raw task data, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and field decisions. 3 Table planner Interactive table builder for fields, data types, keys, and example values. 4 ERD studio Interactive ERD builder with relationship mapping and diagram output. 5 Test plan Create a project test table before coding begins.

Turn separate tables into one model

The ERD is where the class proves the tables actually belong together. Every line on the diagram should match a relationship you could explain as a sentence about the client system.

If a relationship cannot be justified from the brief, it probably does not belong in version one.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
One-to-oneOne record in a table links to one record in another.
One-to-manyOne parent record can link to many child records.
Many-to-manyBoth sides can link to multiple records, so a linking table is needed.
Referential integrityLinked records remain valid and consistent.

Relationship rules

  • A foreign key should point to a real parent key you can identify clearly.
  • If you cannot express the relationship as a sentence, the ERD is not ready yet.
  • The original SQL model should include only the core entities. Tagging comes later.
